nav.home_description:
ONDA Life is a practice of self-awareness and body awareness.

Connect your tracker or smartwatch in settings and observe how your vital signs change during practice in real time.

The greater your success in completing practices — your time in practice and improvement in your state — the more OND in your account. A connected tracker or smartwatch will also increase your earnings for completing practices.

When all practices of a part are completed with more than 40% success, you unlock the next level.

At the beginning of each part before Main practices you will see general guidance. At the end of each part – more detailed attunement to the current state of practices.

In the Emotional Check window you will learn your current emotional state and can complete an Adaptive practice.

And remember that the ONDA level system is a long chain of realizations through feeling yourself as an amoeba, fish, animal, primate, human, brain cell, DNA, and finally, an atom. But if you give due attention to each stage, your journey will be easy and fulfilling.

Good luck on your journey!

circuits.title: Consciousness Circuits
circuits.circuit_1_desc:
Awareness of the very fact of presence.
No tasks, no goals — just the feeling of "I am alive"
Point of zero effort, the first breath of the Universe.
circuits.circuit_2_desc:
Awareness of movement and direction through flow.
Not a route, not a goal — only the feeling of "I swim".
Point of the first impulse, the first wave of movement.
circuits.circuit_5_desc:
Awareness of strength and space.
Not attack, not defense — a clear feeling: 'I am here, and this is my place'.
A point of calm dominance, where power needs no proof.
circuits.circuit_6_desc:
Awareness of connection and presence among others.
Not dissolution, not domination — the ability to be in the field.
A point of social balance, where emotions become language.
circuits.circuit_7_subtitle: The Observing Human / Clarity and Discernment
circuits.circuit_7_desc:
Awareness of differences and forms.
Not evaluation, not analysis — the ability to see what is what.
The birth point of mind, where the world ceases to be a continuous stream.
circuits.circuit_8_subtitle: The Gathering Human / Attention and Concentration
circuits.circuit_8_desc:
Awareness of attention direction.
Not tension, not control — the ability to hold what is chosen.
The point of concentration, where thought ceases to scatter.
circuits.circuit_9_subtitle: The Creating Human / Architect of Inner Projections
circuits.circuit_9_desc:
Awareness of the power of imagination and synthesis.
Not just data processing — the ability to see the whole in empty space.
The point of cognitive breakthrough, where mind learns to design the future.
circuits.circuit_10_subtitle: The Social Human / Master of Manifestation
circuits.circuit_10_desc:
Awareness of your role and value in society.
Not just transmitting sounds — but conveying your inner image outward.
The point of social birth, where you announce your presence to the world.
circuits.circuit_11_subtitle: The Social Human / Master of Resonance
circuits.circuit_11_desc:
Awareness of the value of exchange and partnership.
Not just contact — but the ability to hear the world's responsive impulse.
The point of social balance, where your 'I want' meets another person's 'I want'.
circuits.circuit_12_subtitle: The Cultural Human / Master of Synergy
circuits.circuit_12_desc:
Awareness of the power of collective creation.
Not just working together — but the alchemy of shared meanings and goals.
The highest point of social maturity, where you become the architect of a common future.
circuits.circuit_4_desc:
Awareness of mobility and reaction.
Not attack, not freezing — the ability to change trajectory.
A point of living adaptation, where movement is born before thought.
circuits.circuit_3_desc:
Mastery of two worlds: water's fluidity + earth's support.
Not fight or flight — adapting form to conditions.
Point of balance: first stable step and breath between two worlds.

practice_messages.breath_message: Inhale — attention to the center of the body, exhale — gentle glow from within. Feel the breath as life.
practice_messages.being_message: Sit for 3 minutes, just observing the breath. Realize "I am" without action.
practice_messages.pulse_message: Place your hand on your belly or heart, feel the warmth. Feel life in your body.
practice_messages.still_message: Feel breath as movement within stillness.
practice_messages.listening_message: Close your eyes and listen to body sounds (pulse, breath). Listen to your body.
practice_messages.light_message: On inhale — light gathers in the center, on exhale — spreads through the body. Awaken inner light.
practice_messages.liquid_message: Imagine you are a drop of water; move diffusely without effort. Feel yourself as liquid.
practice_messages.count_message: Count 10 breath cycles without losing awareness. Focus attention on breath.
practice_messages.stillness_message: Feel a point of stillness inside your body. Find the center of perception.
practice_messages.silence_message: 6 minutes without thoughts or movements — just being. Experience pure presence.
practice_messages.ground_message: Inhale — into chest, exhale — into the earth through feet. Connect heaven and earth through body.
practice_messages.root_message: Feel the weight of your body. From the base of your spine, roots grow deep into the earth. With each exhale, roots go deeper. You are a tree.
practice_messages.flow_rhythm_message: Enter the rhythm of water: inhale — meet the wave, exhale — follow it.
practice_messages.directional_sense_message: Find the easy line of movement: where the body feels lighter — that's the right direction.
practice_messages.rhythm_movement_message: Connect breath and wave: inhale — gather yourself, exhale — glide.
practice_messages.water_balance_message: Stand softly. Knees spring. Inhale — axis, exhale — support.
practice_messages.fluid_motion_message: Become water: round your movements, soften angles, breathe smoothly.
practice_messages.wave_breath_message: Inhale — wave rises, exhale — gentle retreat. Listen to the ocean inside your chest.
practice_messages.sense_of_flow_message: Let the mind be still. Let the body indicate the direction of ease.
practice_messages.flow_focus_message: Choose one point of gaze. Move softly — stay here.
practice_messages.flow_adapt_message: Maintain center. Allow body to softly adjust trajectory.
practice_messages.still_water_message: Reduce movement to almost zero. Listen to silence beneath the wave of breath.
practice_messages.deep_current_message: Listen not to waves, but to the low underwater current — it guides from within.
practice_messages.echo_ocean_message: Inhale — call, exhale — answer. Become quieter to hear the ocean within.
practice_messages.breath_of_transition_message: Inhale — water, exhale — earth. Breathe two worlds.
practice_messages.balance_point_message: Inhale — gather axis, exhale — anchor support. Center — above mid-foot.
practice_messages.adaptive_flow_message: Center remains — form changes. Be water in clay.
practice_messages.ground_air_breath_message: Inhale — to sky, exhale — to the earth. Center remains calm.
practice_messages.step_of_stability_message: Maintain axis. Weight — in support. Step is born from exhale.
practice_messages.wave_of_breath_message: Inhale — wave rises up spine, exhale — descends into feet.
practice_messages.breath_bridge_message: Inhale — gather (water), exhale — root (earth). Between them — bridge.
practice_messages.center_of_gravity_message: Place attention in lower belly. Breathe so weight stands at mid-foot.
practice_messages.shape_shift_message: Center — in place, form — for the task. Breathe and change softly.
practice_messages.resonant_stillness_message: Freeze steadily. Breath — quiet, exhale slightly longer. Listen to silence beneath breath.
practice_messages.pulse_of_earth_message: Listen to low rhythm under feet: inhale — gathers, exhale — goes into depth.
practice_messages.breath_of_adaptation_message: Inhale — accept conditions, exhale — strengthen support. Find your working rhythm.
practice_messages.soft_gaze_message: Let your eyes look not at a point — but into space. Let the world unfold before you.
practice_messages.orienting_inhale_message: Inhale sharply and keenly, as if trying to catch a faint scent of change. Let this breath bring you back from the labyrinth of thoughts to the real world.
practice_messages.audio_scan_message: Become hearing itself. Let the sounds of the world pass through you without touching your feelings — as if you're tuning a sensitive instrument to the frequency of silence.
practice_messages.mammalian_neck_message: Let your head move softly and freely, like a keen animal in a quiet forest. Let the tension flow away, opening the path to your clarity.
practice_messages.tail_reset_message: Feel your spine not as a rigid rod, but as a living, flowing stem. Let the wave of relaxation rise from the very roots of your body.
practice_messages.lymphatic_drift_message: Become fluid and weightless. Let a gentle wave of vibration wash away the remnants of fatigue and tension from every cell.
practice_messages.deep_in_quick_out_message: Shed the weight of the frozen moment. Let air into your deepest self and exhale resolve, making room for new movement.
practice_messages.distance_barrier_message: The world ends where you begin. Feel the transparent but strong sphere of your presence and let it become your personal fortress.
practice_messages.trajectory_detection_message: Stop seeing faces and details. Start seeing vectors, speeds, and directions. Become a point of stillness through which the flow of trajectories passes.
practice_messages.shadow_maneuvering_message: Imagine the air around you is filled with invisible strings. Slip through them, maintaining the sensitivity and lightness of every movement.
practice_messages.sensory_bypass_message: Hand control over to your body. Let your feet find the path on their own, while your mind remains clear and free from calculations.
practice_messages.tonic_fluidity_message: Become a master of your states. Learn to switch your inner power with a single impulse of will, leaving no inertia to old emotions.
practice_messages.mass_center_message: Feel your inner gravity. When you have weight, the world stops swaying you — you become the reference point.
practice_messages.vagal_brake_message: Press pause. Calm your pulse and return to a point of absolute calm, using direct levers of control over your biology.
practice_messages.lymphatic_lock_message: Break the stagnation inside you. Let the deep pressure of the diaphragm become a pump that washes away anxiety and returns purity and lightness to the body.
practice_messages.gravity_grounding_message: Stop resisting gravity — let it become your strength. Become heavy, become part of the earth, become the one who cannot be moved.
practice_messages.testosterone_vertical_message: Stretch your power into a line. Become a bridge between earth and sky, turning your posture into an undeniable manifesto of calm power.
practice_messages.protected_heart_message: Find your anchor point. Let the warmth of your hand create a zone of absolute peace where your feelings and your strength are born.
practice_messages.silent_roar_message: Give your strength a voice. Let the low vibration of your body fill the space, securing your right to territory and silence.
practice_messages.territorial_gaze_message: Look not at the world, but through it. Your gaze is not a search for threats, it's an inventory of your domain.
practice_messages.heart_coherence_message: Tune your inner frequency. When your heart beats in the rhythm of harmony, someone else's chaos is powerless against your calm.
practice_messages.solid_aura_message: Feel where the world ends and you begin. Densify the space around your heart and center, creating a zone of absolute inviolability.
practice_messages.tigers_path_message: Don't walk on the surface — press into it. Every step you take is a seal confirming your power over the space.
practice_messages.bears_circle_message: Draw your world. Inside this circle you are the highest law and the point of peace. Let every step seal the boundaries of your undeniable influence.
practice_messages.social_breathing_message: Drop the settings of separation. Find a common rhythm where 'I' and 'You' disappear, and a unified field of safe interaction is born.

p1_1:
Feel the breath as life.
Inhale — attention to the center of the body.
Exhale — gentle glow from within.

Let the body find its own rhythm.
Don't control the breath — observe it.

Each inhale connects you with Earth.
Each exhale returns you to peace.

Simply be in the breath.
It breathes in you, and you breathe in it.
p1_2: Sit comfortably. Allow breath to become natural.

Don't seek anything. Don't fix.
Simply observe — inhale, exhale, pause.
Feel that life happens by itself.

In each inhale — birth,
in each exhale — return.

Feel simple presence.
Nothing needs to be achieved — you already are.

All that exists now — breath, body, peace.
Let awareness gently rest inside.
p1_3: Place your hand on your belly or heart.
Feel the beating under your palm. This is the pulse of life — ancient, reliable, real.
Inhale — warmth gathers inside. Exhale — it softly spreads through the body.
Allow the heart to breathe with Earth. Don't rush. Just listen to the rhythm.
Each beat is "I live". Each exhale is "I feel".
Let the body remember how to be alive.
p1_4: All living things sway — even in stillness there is a wave.

Take a breath — and feel the body gently expand.
Exhale — and the world becomes quieter.

Let everything slow down.
No rush, no goal.
Only soft flow inside.

Feel how the the breath becomes almost invisible,
but continues to connect you with life.

In this stillness there is strength.
In this silence — the movement of the world.
p1_5:
Close your eyes.
Let silence enter inside.

Listen not to sounds, but to the space between them.
There lives breath, beating, whisper of life.

Feel how the the the heart sounds in the body.
How lungs answer it with gentle rhythm.

Listen to micro-movements — warmth, pulsation, energy flow.
All this is the body's language, saying: "I am alive".

Don't try to analyze. Just listen.
The body knows how peace sounds.
Let attention dissolve in this inner music.
p1_6: Take a breath and feel light gathering in the center of the chest.
It's small — like a spark, like a point of warmth.

Exhale — and this spark gently spreads through the body.
Let breath become light moving through you.

Inhale — gather light.
Exhale — share it.

Feel how the the the body fills with radiance from within.
Light doesn't come from outside — it's remembered from the depths.
Notice how with each breath the inner space becomes more transparent.

Let attention gently rest in the chest.
Where warm pulse connects you with Earth and sky.

Inhale — like sunrise.
Exhale — like gentle evening.

Let breath become movement of light in the body.
Let each cell softly respond to this radiance.
Don't strive to make light brighter — just allow it to be.

It knows its rhythm.
It knows the path from heart to every part of you.
Feel that in this moment everything is illuminated from within.

Even silence glows.
Even peace breathes with light.
p1_7:
Feel the body.
Imagine it's not solid, but fluid.
As if each cell is filled with soft, warm water.
Take a breath — water rises, fills chest, shoulders, arms.
Exhale — and the flow softly descends to belly, to feet.

Feel how the the breath becomes tide and ebb.
Everything inside moves smoothly, without effort.
Allow the body to dissolve in its own breath.

Inhale — you gather into one wave.
Exhale — you spread in space.

All that's solid becomes mobile.
All that's tense turns into fluidity.

Feel liquid moving under the skin.
As if water carries attention, cleansing and enlivening the body.

No "self", no "body" — only movement of life.
I am form of water, breathing light.

If attention freezes — just gently return it to movement.
Each breath — a wave.
Each pause — peace between tides.

Allow Earth to feel your flow.
Allow yourself to feel Earth through it.

Everything flows.
Everything is connected.
Everything lives by water's breath.
p1_8: Sit calmly. Allow breath to go naturally.

Feel how the the the inhale is born by itself —
and how the exhale completes it without effort.

Start counting breaths —
inhale one, exhale one.
Inhale two, exhale two.

Count gently, without tension.
Let numbers be not with mind, but with breath.

If attention wanders — simply return to the next inhale.
Don't judge yourself, don't rush.
Each new breath is a beginning.
Feel how the the with each count the mind becomes more transparent.

Numbers dissolve, rhythm remains.
Counting becomes breath's music.

Inhale — gentle filling of body.
Exhale — soft descent of attention.

When you breathe consciously, breath becomes support.
It holds you, as Earth holds a seed.

Feel the simplicity of the moment.
One inhale, one exhale.

All that's needed — to be here, in this rhythm.
No end, no goal, only breath and peace.

You and breath are one whole.
Counting is simply form of presence.

Let each inhale sound like the word "I".
And each exhale — like the word "AM".
p1_9:
Close your eyes.
Take a few soft breaths.
Feel how the the with each exhale the body becomes quieter.

Somewhere deep inside there's a point,
where nothing happens — no movement, no thought.
Don't seek it. Allow it to manifest itself.

Inhale — attention gathers in the center.
Exhale — dissolves everything extra.

Inside inhale — peace.
Inside exhale — peace.
Between them — silence.

Feel how the the time slows down.
Everything inside gently stops,
but life continues — without your participation.

Feel the center of perception — motionless axis in the body's depth.
Everything revolves around it,
but it itself remains unchanged.

This is not a place and not an image —
it's presence without form.
The less you try, the clearer it sounds.

Let breath become a whisper.
Let attention descend into the root of silence.

Here there's no "I" and "world" —
there's only peace from which breath is born.

Feel that in this peace — there's strength.
In this silence — source of movement.
All you seek is already breathing inside this point.
p1_10:
Sit comfortably.
Feel how the the breath becomes invisible.

No need to breathe deeper.
No need to control.
Everything already happens by itself.
Allow the body to be motionless.

Feel that inside this stillness
breath continues to move —
gently, like whisper of time.

Don't listen to breath — be it.
Don't observe silence — become it.

Everything extra dissolves.
Words, thoughts, forms — become transparent.

Only awareness remains.
It's without boundaries, without name, without beginning.

Body — simply Earth's breath.
Mind — reflection of space.
All that is — presence.

Feel how the the from within rises gentle light.
It doesn't move — simply is.

Breathe this light.
Be light that listens to itself.

No more "I" and "silence" —
there's only breath that knows itself.

In this breath — peace.
In this peace — life.
In this life — you.
p1_11:
Stand steadily. Feel your feet.
Expand contact with the earth — as if soles become wider and heavier.

Inhale — raise attention from feet to chest.
Feel how the the warm space opens in the center.

Exhale — direct everything down, through legs, into the earth.
Imagine how roots of light grow from feet.

With each inhale — chest fills with warmth.
With each exhale — roots go deeper, finding water and stone.
Don't hurry. Let gravity do the work for you.

Inhale — gather strength in chest, straighten shoulders, become taller.
Exhale — release tension downward: knees soft, jaw free, belly warm.

Feel weight, but as support, not obstacle.
Earth holds you.

If mind goes into thoughts — return to the soles of your feet.
Right here — your support and home.

Inhale — like a ray from heart to sky.
Exhale — like a river going to planet's core.

Roots branch out, embrace soil, intertwine with its pulse.
You stand, and world breathes through you.

Feel how the the confidence rises from bottom up:
feet → shins → pelvis → belly → chest → throat → crown.

Let the body become trunk, and breath — sap.
Strength is not in tension, but in connection.

You are a tree: tall with breath, deep with roots.
Here it's safe. Here you're home.
p1_12:
Stand steadily. Feel feet completely — heels, pads, toes.
Allow weight to descend. Knees soft, pelvis gets heavier.

Transfer attention to the base of spine.
Feel warm point in pelvis center — your root.

Inhale — chest gently opens, spine lengthens, crown reaches toward sky.
Exhale — release everything down the spine, through thighs and shins to feet.

Imagine from the base of spine and from feet
roots grow — warm, alive, feeling.

With each exhale roots go deeper, find moist soil, stone, water.
With each inhale from the earth rises calmness and support.

Allow jaw to relax, shoulders to get heavy and descend.
Breathe like a tree: trunk — your spine, sap — your breath.

If attention goes into thoughts — return to the soles.
Notice floor pressure, temperature, micro-movements in toes.

Expand roots to the sides — forward, back, left, right —
until invisible network of support emerges around you.

Inhale — gather strength in chest center.
Exhale — direct it down, strengthen roots, trust the earth.

Feel boundaries of your space:
"Here I stand. Here is my home. Here I can be heavy and real".

The deeper the roots — the freer the breath,
the quieter the mind, the clearer the heart.

Feel how the the breath guides movement.
p2_2: Find the easy line of movement.

p2_4: Water carries but doesn't knock down.

p3_1: Stand steadily: feet supported, knees soft, axis long.
On inhale imagine cool, flowing water filling sides and back; chest becomes wider.
On exhale direct attention down — through belly, pelvis and legs — warm weight goes into the earth.
Keep rhythm 4–6: inhale shorter, exhale longer — this way transition stabilizes.
Feel how the the water gives fluidity on inhale, and earth gives support on exhale.
If tension appears in throat or shoulders — soften exhale and return weight to feet.
Do several cycles 'water → earth', then reduce effort to almost imperceptible movement, leaving only sensation of element shift.
Check center: belly warm, lower back soft, gaze calm.
Finish with three breaths emphasizing exhale down — anchor support.
p3_2: Stand softly: feet hip-width. Find 'triangle of foot': heel — base of big toe — base of little toe.
Knees spring, pelvis neutral, crown reaches up — like flexible thread.
Place palm on lower belly and note warm center point (slightly below navel).
Do micro-scan forward/back and left/right — amplitude 5%.
Where exhale becomes longer and warmer — there's your 'zero'.
Inhale — axis lengthens; exhale — weight evenly distributes across triangle of feet.
Check pressure balance: heel ↔ ball of big toe ↔ ball of little toe — no tilts.
Soften shoulders and jaw, tongue free; gaze soft, on 'horizon'.
If swaying — reduce amplitude and lengthen exhale (4–6), return attention to feet.
Maintain 1% living movement — balance doesn't freeze, it breathes.
Repeat anchor: belly center warm, spine long, feet wide. Here — your stability.
p3_3: Stand softly: feet hip-width, knees spring, belly warm — this is your center.
Inhale — gather axis; exhale — soften movement edges.
Imagine joints filled with warm liquid: melt knees, pelvis, shoulders, neck.
Explore three basic forms: elongation (longer), rounding (softer), spiral (more plastic).
On inhale — elongate in chosen form; on exhale — round and return to center.
Change form by body/environment signal: where breath is easier — there's adaptation.
Keep amplitude 5–10%: movement almost invisible, but felt from inside.
Center doesn't wander: palm on belly reminds — axis stays, only contours change.
If 'hard angle' appears — pause on exhale and melt it with attention.
Combine forms: elongation → spiral → rounding → center (one breath cycle per phase).
With each cycle simplify: less force, more fluidity; less speed, more feeling.
Finish with several breaths in neutral pose — plasticity preserved, center calm.
p3_4: Stand or sit steadily: feet supported, crown reaches up, shoulders soft.
Place one palm on chest, other on lower belly.
Inhale: feel cool, light air — chest and collarbones expand up and to sides.
Exhale: direct attention down — through belly, pelvis and legs into earth; weight becomes warmer and heavier.
Keep rhythm 4–6: inhale shorter, exhale longer — this brings stability.
Stay several cycles in image: 'sky fills — earth receives'.
Check axis: on inhale it lengthens, on exhale weighs down to feet.
If breathing becomes noisy — soften inhale, keep long warm exhale.
Notice how with each exhale jaw, shoulders, belly calm down.
Reduce effort: inhale like feather, exhale like root.
At end do three calm exhales emphasizing feet — anchor support.
p3_5: Stand steadily: feet hip-width, knees soft, axis long.
Feel weight of body: pelvis heavy, spine vertical, crown to sky.
Inhale — gather axis; exhale — send weight down through one leg.
On long exhale shift weight 100% to one foot — slowly, like root growing.
Free leg becomes light; lift it slightly off floor — 2–3 cm, no higher.
Hold balance: inhale — stabilize axis, exhale — strengthen support.
Place free foot forward or to side — gently, toe first, then heel.
Transfer weight to new foot on exhale — smooth, connected, without rush.
Repeat: step is born from exhale, support — from inhale.
If balance shakes — pause, lengthen exhale, return attention to supporting foot.
Do 5–7 slow steps, keeping warm center in belly.
Finish standing on both feet — feel how earth holds you.
p3_6: Stand softly: feet hip-width, knees soft, crown up.
On inhale imagine warm wave rising from tailbone up spine to crown.
On exhale wave descends — through belly, pelvis, legs into feet.
Keep rhythm 4–6: inhale lifts wave, exhale sends it down.
Feel spine as flexible channel: breath flows through it like water.
Soften shoulders, free jaw; let wave move spine naturally.
If lower back tightens — reduce amplitude, breathe into belly.
Imagine: inhale — spine is river flowing up, exhale — waterfall down.
Keep feet as roots: warm, wide, deeply connected to earth.
With each exhale roots go deeper, support becomes more reliable.
Repeat 7–10 cycles, then simplify to almost imperceptible wave.
Finish with three exhales into feet — anchor stability.
p3_7: Stand or sit comfortably: spine vertical, feet connected to earth.
On inhale imagine light, flowing water filling chest and back — fluidity.
On exhale direct attention down — through belly and legs into earth — density.
Keep rhythm 4–6: inhale gathers like water, exhale roots like earth.
Feel transition point: where water meets earth — that's your center.
Breathe so each phase is distinct: inhale — lightness, exhale — weight.
If confusion appears — pause on exhale, feel feet, then continue.
Imagine bridge between two worlds: upper — fluid, lower — stable.
Your body is meeting point: breath connects what seems separate.
Soften jaw and shoulders; let bridge be natural, not forced.
Repeat 7–10 cycles, notice how both elements live in you simultaneously.
Finish with three exhales down — strengthen earth side of bridge.
p3_8: Stand with feet hip-width, knees soft.
Place attention in lower belly (2 fingers below navel) — your center of gravity.
On inhale feel how center warms and stabilizes.
On exhale send weight down through legs — feel it settling at mid-foot.
Check that weight doesn't shift to toes or heels — stay in middle.
Keep rhythm 4–6: long exhale strengthens stability.
Imagine plumb line from crown through belly center to mid-foot.
If you sway — reduce amplitude, breathe into belly, connect to feet.
Soften shoulders and jaw; gaze soft on horizon.
Feel how the the with each exhale center lowers and stabilizes.
Do micro-sway test: if center is right, any direction feels equally easy.
Finish with palm on belly — remember this place of stability.
p3_9: Stand with warm center in belly, axis long.
Inhale — gather axis; exhale — allow form to shift slightly.
Explore changing orientation: turn body left/right, tilt forward/back — 5–10°.
Keep center fixed: palm on belly reminds — here's your anchor.
Change form on exhale — smooth, without jerks.
Return to neutral on inhale — gather yourself back to axis.
If balance wobbles — reduce amplitude, lengthen exhale.
Try different forms: squat slightly, reach up, spiral — center stays.
Soften jaw, keep feet wide and warm.
Repeat: form serves task, but center never leaves home.
Finish standing neutral — feel how center remained unmoved.
p3_10: Stand or sit in most stable position.
Reduce all external movement to almost zero.
Breathe quietly: inhale minimal, exhale slightly longer (4–6).
Notice natural pause after exhale — that's where stillness lives.
Soften face, jaw, shoulders; let tongue be heavy.
Place attention in three supports: feet/sit bones → belly → heart.
If thought creates movement — note it, return to pause after exhale.
Feel that within stillness life continues to pulse gently.
Don't chase silence — let it settle around you like snow.
Listen for micro-pulse: heartbeat, breath echo, subtle vibration.
Stay several minutes — stillness becomes tangible, like substance.
Finish slowly: first deepen breath, then allow small movement.
p3_11: Stand or sit, feet connected to floor/ground.
Place attention in feet soles and lower belly.
On inhale imagine slow, deep current rising from earth.
On exhale current flows down through you back into depths.
Breathe low: expand sides and lower back; upper body free.
Soften shoulders and jaw; let weight drain into support.
If mind goes to surface (thoughts, noise) — return to low warm current in belly.
Keep rhythm 4–6 or slower — Earth's pulse is measured.
Check axis: crown up, sacrum down; current flows along spine.
Reduce visible movement to almost zero, keep sensation of deep flow.
Let this current 'carry' attention — effortless but steady.
Maintain foot contact: depth always finds path to earth.
p3_12: Stand in your current environment — don't seek ideal conditions.
On inhale accept what is: temperature, sounds, sensations.
On exhale send weight down, strengthen connection to earth.
Breathe with environment rhythm: if noisy — exhale longer, if cold — breathe into belly.
Don't fight conditions — adjust form while keeping center.
If uncomfortable — micro-shift position on exhale, find new stability.
Keep feet warm and wide; let earth be constant while everything else changes.
Soften jaw and shoulders; adaptation happens through release, not tension.
Repeat: inhale accepts, exhale anchors — this is your working rhythm.
Notice how body finds solutions when you stop insisting.
Stay several minutes, let new form settle.
Finish knowing: environment is not obstacle, it's information for adaptation.
p4_1: Choose a point in front of you, but don't 'stare' at it with attention.
Soften your gaze, as if looking through a transparent veil or into deep twilight.
Without moving your pupils, slowly begin to notice the right and left edges of space.
Allow your attention to flow to the sides, embracing walls, shadows, and air beside you.
Your gaze is no longer a 'tunnel' seeking a target; now it's a wide, calm mirror.
Feel how, with the expansion of your field of view, the ancient fear in the depths of your brain quiets.
The tension of 'hunting' fades, the frozen expectation of 'prey' dissolves.
You no longer fixate on details — you monitor life itself in its wholeness.
Breathe freely, holding both edges of space in your attention simultaneously.
Notice how, along with the defocus of eyes, your jaw and back of head relax.
Your brain is switching: from anxious searching — to safe presence.
Stay in this volumetric world, where there are no targets, only pure being.
Keep this panorama inside, even when focus returns to tasks.
p4_2: Freeze for a moment, wherever you are.
Imagine you are an explorer in an unfamiliar but interesting space.
Take a series of sharp, short inhales through your nose — as if actively 'sniffing the air'.
Feel how the cool stream touches the upper parts of your nasopharynx.
Once more: two or three short 'sniff-breaths', eagerly and curiously.
Listen as silence sets in inside at this moment: your brain is busy analyzing the environment.
This 'sniff' breaks the thread of anxious dialogue, returning you to 'here and now'.
Feel how your pupils become sharper, and your hearing — keener.
You are no longer a victim of your feelings; you are an active observer, studying the world.
Notice three scents or simply the feeling of freshness around you.
Let this impulse of curiosity displace the remnants of emotional fog.
Breathe calmly now, but keep this sharp edge of attention.
p4_3: Close your eyes or simply lower your eyelids, shutting out visual noise.
Imagine your ears are highly sensitive direction finders, capable of catching the universe's whisper.
First, hear the sounds of your body: your breathing, the beat of blood, the quiet rustle of clothing.
Now expand your sphere of attention: find the loudest or closest sound in the space around you.
Don't name it, don't judge it — just acknowledge its presence and move on.
Now — the most important part: find the quietest, barely perceptible sound in this room.
Grab onto it with your attention, hold it for a second, like a thin thread.
Take another step: send your hearing outward, beyond the walls. Find the most distant sound — on the street, in the sky, beyond the horizon.
Feel how your brain quickly switches filters, jumping from near to far, from obvious to hidden.
You are an impartial observer. Sounds simply exist, and they have no power over your calm.
Notice how in the pauses between sounds, your own inner silence is born.
The reticular formation of your brain is now clear and ready to work, cutting off everything unnecessary.
p4_4: Lower your shoulders and feel the weight of your arms; let them pull the tension down, toward the earth.
Imagine your nose is the tip of a fine brush, barely touching an invisible canvas.
Begin slowly tracing a smooth horizontal 'figure eight' in the air with your nose.
Move smoothly and silently, like a graceful animal maintaining full maneuverability.
Feel the ice melting where the skull meets the spine — where anxiety hides.
Your neck is no longer a frozen shell; it's a living, flexible bridge between body and mind.
With each loop of the 'figure eight', vessels open up, allowing blood to flow to the prefrontal cortex.
Feel how the back of your head becomes light, and the inner space of your head — bright and spacious.
Reduce the amplitude to a barely noticeable whisper; let the movement become almost imaginary.
Notice how along with the neck muscles, the root of the tongue and muscles around the eyes relax.
Your vestibular system finds the point of perfect balance, giving you support in motion.
Stay in this feeling of fluid strength, where there's no place for tension, only free energy.
p4_5: Feel your tailbone — the point of support and the beginning of your inner freedom.
Imagine you have a long, soft tail touching the ground itself.
Begin a barely noticeable, microscopic movement of your pelvis.
As if you're gently swaying this imaginary tail.
Let this impulse turn into a soft wave that begins to crawl up your vertebrae.
The wave travels from the pelvis to the lower back, higher to the shoulder blades, reaching the base of the skull.
This movement is almost invisible from the outside, but inside it feels like melting ice.
With each micro-movement of the 'tail', static tension accumulated over hours flows down into the earth.
Feel how your spine becomes flexible, like seaweed in deep, calm water.
Your body is no longer a compressed spring; it's a living, pulsating wave.
Relax your sacrum, release your lower back. Let energy flow freely, without obstacles.
Imagine this wave washing away the weight of responsibility and others' expectations from your back.
Breathe in rhythm with this movement, feeling how with each cycle your body becomes lighter and more supple.
p4_6: Stand straight, feet parallel, knees slightly relaxed and springy.
Slightly rise on your toes and begin a small, frequent vibration throughout your body.
Imagine you're not made of stone and bones, but of soft, pliable jelly.
Let this vibration rise from your heels to your calves, thighs, and pelvis.
Shake softly, without effort, as if you're the surface of water into which a stone was thrown.
Feel how your shoulders, cheeks, and even tongue relax. Let your whole body 'drift' in this rhythm.
Imagine thousands of tiny pumps starting inside, pushing lymph through the vessels.
Each movement washes toxins and stagnant emotions from the tissues, transforming them into pure energy.
Without lifting your feet from the floor, let your body sway slightly and flow in different directions while maintaining the inner tremor.
Feel the pleasant warmth spreading across your skin — this is a sign that cleansing has begun.
Breathe deeply and freely, helping your body renew with each cycle of vibration.
Gradually reduce the intensity until the movement becomes a barely perceptible hum inside.
p4_7: Place one hand on your belly — feel the center of your stability.
Take a deep, slow inhale through your nose, directing air into the very depths of your belly.
Feel how your belly rounds, filling with the power of the earth.
Now — a short, sharp, but soft exhale through your mouth.
As if extinguishing a candle with one precise movement.
Inhale — quiet and low, like the tide of the ocean.
Exhale — clear and quick, like a switch clicking.
With each short exhale, shed the remnants of anxiety like dust from clothing.
Feel how an impulse to action is born inside, free from fuss.
You are no longer a 'frozen target' — you are a flow, ready to change direction.
Deep inhale again — slowly fill the base of your body, like a cup.
And a sharp exhale — like a whip crack, cutting off everything unnecessary.
Relax your shoulders on the exhale, but keep tone in your feet and palms.
Breathe as if you're starting the engine of your intention.
Feel clarity in your head and springy readiness in your body.
You control this rhythm, which means — you control the situation.
p4_8: Stand or sit straight. Imagine a transparent sphere around you at arm's length.
This is your sacred space — a zone where you are completely in control.
Feel the density of air inside this sphere. It's warm, calm, and belongs to you.
Imagine an object or person slowly entering this space.
Notice how your body instantly reacts with micro-tension.
Don't freeze. Gently 'roll back' with attention or micro-movement, keeping your sphere's shape intact.
Learn to change the boundaries of your zone: expand them when you feel strong, and compress them when protection is needed.
Let the muscles inside the sphere stay relaxed. All protection lies in the awareness of the boundary itself.
Breathe deeply, filling your 'bubble' of safety with confidence and silence.
If someone pushes on your boundaries, imagine your sphere becoming elastic, like rubber, gently repelling foreign influence.
You are the center of this space. Everything outside is just information. Everything inside is your unshakeable integrity.
Feel the ground with your feet: your sphere is rooted. It cannot be moved without your consent.
p4_9: Relax your gaze, as in the 'Soft Gaze' practice, but don't close your eyes.
Look through people and objects, as if they are transparent ghosts in space.
Focus only on movement. Catch vectors: someone accelerates, someone changes angle, someone slows down.
Don't look at faces — faces carry emotions that steal your resources. Look at body trajectories.
Perceive the world as a flow of colored lines crossing the space around you.
Your task is simply to note directions: left to right, fast, slow, in an arc.
Feel how your inner critic and evaluator quiets down.
There's no 'good' or 'bad' here, only dynamics.
You are an impartial processor, processing a map of speeds and trajectories.
Notice how your body naturally begins to adjust to this rhythm, becoming streamlined and ready to maneuver.
Stay in this state of 'transparent observer', for whom only the rhythm and direction of flow matters.
Feel the lightness: when the world is a flow of trajectories, it's impossible to get stuck or lost in it.
p4_10: Begin moving slowly, imagining the space is threaded with laser beams or thin cobwebs.
Your task is not to touch any of them. Move smoothly, flowing around invisible obstacles.
Change levels: crouch slightly, dodge with your shoulder, let an imaginary thread pass over your head.
Feel the difference between 'tension' and 'readiness'. Your muscles are like violin strings: alive, but not clamped.
Let movement originate in the center of your body and spread to your fingertips.
Each step is a dance of maneuverability. You're always in balance, even in the moment of changing pose.
Imagine you're a shadow gliding along a wall. Intangible, fluid, fast.
Breathe in rhythm with your dodges: inhale — expansion, exhale — smooth glide past the obstacle.
Train your cerebellum: feel the space behind you, beside you, under your feet.
You're not fighting space — you're playing with it, becoming part of it.
Feel how your brain enjoys this complex and beautiful task, releasing background anxieties.
Freeze for a second in any pose and feel: you're ready to move in any direction in that same second.
p4_11: Begin moving, choosing a target — 'clean' areas of the floor.
Gradually increase speed, not giving yourself time for long deliberation.
Don't look directly at your feet. Use 'soft gaze' and peripheral vision to scan the surface.
Let your body recalculate the trajectory itself. Trust its natural grace and accuracy.
Feel how your feet find safe islands on their own, as if crossing a mountain stream on stones.
Your brain works ahead — it sees an obstacle before you have time to think about it.
Feel the thrill and lightness of this dance. There's no room for error here, only endless adaptation.
Let movements become fluid and fast. You're a stream flowing around stones in a riverbed.
With each step, your confidence in your body's intuition grows.
Notice how the inner noise disappears in this rhythm. Only the pure joy of precise movement remains.
You are one with space. You maneuver in it without effort or tension.

p5_1: Take up space. Spread your shoulders as if your back is a wide rock.
Imagine that in your lower belly, just below the navel, lies a dense, warm, and very heavy block.
This block doesn't press on you — it holds you, connecting you to the very center of the earth.
Begin breathing: a deep inhale for 4 counts, directing air straight into this block.
Feel how your lower belly expands, accepting this volume.
Hold your breath for 2 seconds — lock in your density and mass.
Now — a long, smooth exhale for 8 counts. With this exhale, the block becomes even heavier.
Feel how with each cycle, the 'inner weight' lowers your shoulders and relaxes your face.
You are no longer a feather in the wind. You are a monolith that cannot be moved by a random word or glance.
Breathe into the lower center. Let each exhale wash away the fuss, leaving only cold, calm confidence.
Feel how testosterone fills your tissues, and cortisol melts, turning into pure energy of presence.
Keep this feeling of 'heavy center' even when you start moving or speaking.
p5_2: Close your eyes and gently touch your fingers to your eyelids. The pressure should be gentle, barely noticeable — like touching a petal.
Or find the hollows behind your earlobes. Begin slow circular movements, warming this area.
Feel how with this simple gesture, a 'brake' switches on inside.
Your heart hears this signal and begins to beat slower, calmer, stronger.
Imagine you're turning down the volume on a too-loud radio. The noise of thoughts fades.
The autonomic system switches: from fuss — to contemplation, from defense — to presence.
With each exhale, warmth from the massage or softness in your eyes spreads throughout your body.
You are no longer a prisoner of reaction. You are the one who presses the button and chooses peace.
Stay in this darkness or this warmth for a few more seconds, completely releasing residual tension.

p5_4: Close your eyes for a moment
Feel how gravity gently pulls your body down
Don't hold yourself — give your weight to the chair and floor
Imagine your center of gravity turning into molten lead and flowing down to the very bottom of your pelvis
Feel how your sitting bones firmly 'dig into' the support
You are putting down roots right here and now

Your mass is your power over space
Let your thighs become heavy, your feet — wide and dense

p4_1: Biology: Expanding the field of vision reduces amygdala activity.
Why: This is a motor pattern of environmental monitoring in small mammals, canceling the tunnel vision of 'prey'.
Effect: Reduction of background anxiety levels.
p4_2: Biology: Imitation of the orienting reflex (exploratory behavior).
Why: A sharp inhale through the nose sends a signal to the cerebral cortex, forcibly shifting focus from internal emotions to external stimuli.
Effect: Instant 'sobering' of attention and breaking the cycle of obsessive anxieties.
Bio-marker: Activation of cholinergic systems responsible for selective attention.
p4_3: Biology: Imitation of the orienting reflex through the auditory channel.
Why: Training of signal filtering in the reticular formation of the brainstem.
Effect: Increased cognitive selectivity — the ability to instantly cut out the unnecessary and maintain focus.
Bio-marker: Shift of dominance toward theta rhythms while maintaining high alertness.
p4_4: Biology: Reduction of deep suboccipital muscle tone.
Bio-marker: Optimization of vestibulo-spinal tract function.
Effect: Improved blood supply to the prefrontal cortex.
p4_5: Biology: Activation of parasympathetic response through stimulation of the sacral plexus.
Why: In mammals, tail micro-movements are an evolutionary mechanism for releasing 'frozen' tension after experienced stress.
Effect: Deep muscle relaxation and removal of static block from the body axis.
Bio-marker: Reduced tone in the lumbosacral region and normalization of breathing rhythm.
p4_6: Biology: Stimulation of the lymphatic system through rhythmic muscle contractions.
Why: The lymphatic system has no 'pump' of its own (heart); its movement depends entirely on muscle movement. Vibration is the most effective way to initiate this process.
Effect: Accelerated elimination of stress metabolism products (cortisol, adrenaline) and reduction of swelling.
Bio-marker: Reduced lactate and cortisol concentration in intercellular fluid.
p4_7: Biology: Switching the sympathetic nervous system from 'freeze' mode to 'maneuver' mode.
Why: A sharp but controlled exhale interrupts the freeze cycle, activating resources for an active response to challenge.
Effect: Rapid emotional stabilization and exit from 'mental fog' state.
Bio-marker: Mobilization shift in heart rate variability.
p4_8: Biology: Calibration of peripersonal space in the parietal cortex of the brain.
Why: Distance control is an evolutionary mechanism of mammals that, with clear awareness of boundaries, activates the parasympathetic system (relaxation).
Effect: Strengthening of psychological boundaries, reduction of social anxiety and feelings of vulnerability.
Bio-marker: Reduced cortisol levels while maintaining high stress resistance.
p4_9: Action: Find a safe space in a crowded place (cafe, station, busy street). Can be practiced sitting or standing.
Biology: Activation of the dorsal stream of the visual system (the 'Where?' and 'How?' pathway through the parietal cortex).
Why: Switching attention from objects ('What is it?') to movement vectors disables emotional evaluation and enables pure environmental calculation.
Effect: Accelerated reaction speed to any changes and increased maneuverability in crowds or information flow.
p4_10: Biology: Dynamic modulation of muscle tone through the basal ganglia.
Why: Training the cerebellum and basal ganglia allows the body to instantly adapt to changes without wasting resources on unnecessary tension.
Effect: Increased movement plasticity, improved coordination and sense of balance.
Bio-marker: Optimization of signals from proprioceptors (body position sensors in space).
p4_11: Action: Walk through space, consciously avoiding certain zones (tile lines, carpet edges, shadows, or imaginary spots).
Biology: Stimulation of the superior colliculi and cerebellum for instant automatic movement correction.
Why: Using peripheral vision for navigation disables slow 'conscious' planning and activates ancient, ultra-fast neural circuits.
Effect: Optimization of proprioception and coordination under time pressure; relief of cognitive overload.
p4_12: Biology: Training autonomic flexibility (Vagal Tone).
Why: The ability to quickly switch between branches of the autonomic nervous system prevents burnout and chronic stress.
Effect: Increased adaptability, control over reactions, and the ability to 'switch on' for work without a long warm-up.
Bio-marker: Increase in heart rate variability (HRV) and vagal tone index.
p5_1: Action: Assume a 'power pose': back straight, shoulders open, feet firmly planted on the support.
Biology: Suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. Research confirms that such exposure reduces cortisol by 25% and increases testosterone by 20%.
Bio-marker: Stimulation of the Ventral Vagus. Extended exhale is a direct signal to the brain about safety, stabilizing heart rate variability (HRV).
Effect: A feeling of 'inner weight' emerges — the biological basis of calm dominance.
p5_2: Action: Gently press fingertips on closed eyelids for 10-20 seconds or softly massage the warm area behind the ears (at the base of the skull).
Biology: Activation of parasympathetic tone through cranial nerves (Aschner-Dagnini reflex).
Bio-marker: Reduction in heart rate and normalization of heart rate variability (HRV).
Effect: Instant cooling of the 'emotional engine', transition from anxiety mode to cold calculation mode.
p5_3: Biology: Direct mechanical massage of the cisterna chyli (main lymphatic collector) by diaphragm legs.
Why: Chronic stress causes the diaphragm to spasm, literally 'locking' lymph in the abdominal cavity. This exercise restores drainage.
Effect: The physical sensation of a 'lump in the stomach' disappears, metabolism improves and system detoxification occurs.
p5_4: Action: Sit on a chair, place your feet parallel. Feel the contact points of your body with the seat and floor.
Biology: Activation of proprioceptors and vestibulo-spinal tracts that transmit signals from the inner ear to muscles that maintain posture.
Why: When the brain receives a clear signal of physical stability ('I am standing/sitting firmly'), the limbic system (fear center) automatically reduces its reactivity.
Effect: Fidgeting in movements disappears, voice becomes deeper, gaze — calmer.
p5_5: Biology: Activation of proprioceptive pathways leading to the reticular formation of the brainstem — the center of wakefulness and readiness.
Bio-marker: Balancing somatotropin levels (growth and recovery hormone) and suppression of prolactin (stress submission and defeat hormone).
Effect: Formation of a powerful non-verbal signal 'I am here, I am strong'. Others read this code as a sign of high status and reliability.
p5_6: Physiology: Stimulation of the thymus area (thymus gland) and sternal sensory receptors. This improves neuroimmune regulation, signaling the brain about physical integrity.
Why: In moments of social threat, we instinctively compress the chest. This exercise forcibly shifts biochemistry from 'compression' to 'protected expansion'.
Effect: A deep feeling of 'my zone is calmly protected' appears, emotional vulnerability decreases.
p5_7: Action: Stand in a rooted position (GRAVITY GROUNDING). Take a deep breath into your belly. On the exhale, make a low, dense sound 'OOOMM' or 'RRRRR' coming from the very depths of your belly.
Biomechanics: Activation of the diaphragm and vocal cords, which are directly connected to the vagus nerve.
Bio-marker: Reduction in cortisol levels and stimulation of oxytocin release through rhythmic chest vibration.
Effect: Expression of strength in a socially acceptable way. Releasing blocks from throat and chest, gaining a 'commanding' voice that is listened to without objection.
p5_8: Action: Choose an object in front of you (1-2 meters away), focus on it for 5-8 seconds. Then smoothly shift your gaze to the farthest point beyond it and hold focus for another 5-8 seconds. Repeat the cycle 3 times.
Physiology: Training accommodation and alternating work of the ciliary muscle. This stabilizes the visual system and reduces amygdala activity.
Bio-marker: Transition from 'tunnel vision' (a sign of stress) to panoramic view.
Effect: Reduction of environmental emotional pressure. You begin to perceive space not as hostile, but as belonging to you.
p5_9: Biology: Formation of an ordered electromagnetic field (according to HeartMath Institute research). The heart is the most powerful EM field generator in the body.
Bio-marker: Synchronization of brain rhythms (alpha waves) with heart rate variability.
Effect: A state of 'invulnerability'. Your system operates at its own frequency, so others' anger, panic or pressure cannot resonate with you and 'infect' you.
p5_10: Physiology: Tactile visualization activates the insular cortex (insula) — a key brain node responsible for interoception (sensing processes inside the body) and forming the body boundary schema.
Bio-marker: Enhancement of alpha rhythms signaling a state of protected rest.
Effect: Personality boundaries begin to be felt physically, making your presence 'dense' and natural to others.
p5_11: Biology: Increasing foot-ground contact time maximally activates sole proprioceptors. This sends a super-stability signal to the brain, which automatically inhibits amygdala activity (anxiety center).
Bio-marker: Change in neuromotor gait pattern: reduced step frequency with increased 'density'. This correlates with increased testosterone levels and reduced social anxiety.
Effect: A physical sense of 'your territory' appears. You are no longer a guest in this space — you are its master.
p5_12: Action: Mark a circle on the floor (imaginary or real — with tape, carpet). Slowly walk its perimeter with the 'tiger's path'. Stop at four key points (cardinal directions).
Biomechanics: Territory marking through proprioceptive and visual confirmation of boundaries.
Bio-marker: Maximum reduction of amygdala activity and stabilization of the HPA axis (cortisol-testosterone balance).
Effect: Strengthening the sense of territoriality, total reduction of social anxiety and formation of an 'impenetrable' presence.
p6_1: Action: Sit or stand facing another person (or imagine them).
Physiology: Synchronization of breathing frequency leads to coherence of heart rate variability (HRV) in both participants. This activates the ventral vagus in both simultaneously.
Bio-marker: Reduction of cortisol levels and the beginning of oxytocin production, signaling that the person nearby is 'one of us'.
